items.title: Woodside to axe 500 jobs, sparking fears for WA workers

items.title: Major survey finds Australia's social cohesion under strain

children.content: A new social cohesion report says it has been a "shocking year for Australia", with the Bondi terrorist attack and other instances of intolerance and racism on the rise.

items.title: How the Wegovy pill compares to weight-loss injections

children.content: A new tablet version of Wegovy, a peptide used to help people lose weight, has been approved for the first time in Australia.

items.title: Education ministers agree to biggest school system shake-up in years

children.content: Ministers will enforce a digital detox in schools, establish an antisemitism curriculum and consider mandatory civics classes.

children.content: A 29-year-old Singaporean man is sentenced to more than five years in jail for driving over and killing a man who had stolen his partner's brother's bag in suburban Perth.

items.title: Study finds one third of infants diagnosed with peanut allergy can eat nuts

children.content: A study by the Murdoch Children's Research Institute has found more than one third of infants diagnosed with a peanut allergy may actually be able to tolerate the food.

image.altText: A baby eating.

items.title: Former councillor pleads not guilty to stalking senior shire staff

children.content: A former Shire of Esperance councillor has pleaded not guilty to stalking two employees, including a senior staff member at the local government.

image.altText: Gemma Johnston leaving Esperance Courthouse on Tuesday, November 3.

items.title: Aboriginal affairs minister denies responsibility for WA child protection crisis

children.content: Don Punch commits to visiting Port Hedland, but says he is not directly responsible for growing problems with the protection of the town's vulnerable indigenous children.

image.altText: Don Punch holds a microphone as he addresses an off-camera crowd.

items.title: Meta is training its AI on millions of Australians, but now you can stop it

children.content: Meta has quietly introduced a way for Australians to stop the tech giant from training its AI on their user data, but the company never announced it, leaving the choice effectively hidden for more than a year.

image.altText: A robot head with facebook and Instagram logos coming out of the top.

children.content: Wyndham Youth Aboriginal Corporation gives workers less than a week to move out of employer-provided housing after the organisation experienced financial issues.
